goal: Close the one silence the boundary's decision audit left open. P21C made every authorization decision durably auditable and P21D carried that audit to the ASGI callable, but CreateCustomerPipeline's identityTenantGuard short-circuits before the policy decision point is ever consulted: a request claiming a foreign tenant or a foreign actor was refused with nothing written anywhere, so the one class of request most worth having a record of — an attempted cross-tenant or cross-actor reach — was exactly the class that left no record. This package adds one optional, strictly descriptor-validated auditIdentityGuard collaborator to CreateCustomerPipeline, awaited only after a genuine guard refusal and before that refusal is returned, and injects one durable witness for it inside createAuditedCustomerComposition over the very same decision log, id generator, clock and chain head the audited policy decision point already uses. A pipeline built without the collaborator behaves exactly as it did before, and createCustomerComposition stays unaudited. The fixed expectations stay owned by the frozen test file; this manifest describes the scenarios, binds the provenance and gates the run, and supplies no expected value back to any assertion.

conditionalDeliveryGates.evidence: One problem only: an identity-guard refusal left no record. Every changed line serves that one problem — one optional pipeline collaborator with its own descriptor gate and its one awaited call site, one durable witness inside the audited composition root, one manifest, one frozen test. No unrelated refactor, rename or cleanup rides along.
Exactly the four files named in allowedFiles were touched, declared up front and unchanged since: git status shows two modified sources and two new files and nothing else.

The witness reuses the caller-supplied idGenerator, the existing Clock, the existing DecisionLogPort instance, the existing PostgresDecisionLogAdapter and its bound chainHead, and the existing Command, PolicyRequest, PolicyDecision and DecisionLogEntry value types rather than reimplementing any of them; the one DecisionLogPort the audited policy decision point already used was hoisted and shared instead of a second one being constructed. It duplicates no hashing, chaining, evaluation or persistence logic; no new module, dependency, capability, framework or host was introduced.

No test was weakened, skipped or made conditional; the frozen test was never edited and its hash is unchanged from the handoff snapshot. The optional option is decided from its own property descriptor alone, so an accessor-backed member is refused rather than invoked and a non-enumerable or present-but-undefined member is refused rather than read as absence; the pipeline stays a pure Application-ring value with no fs, net, http, https or crypto import, no fetch, no environment read, no ambient clock and no random value; and the witness is awaited and its refusal propagates unchanged, so an unrecordable deny can never answer an unrecorded 403.

identityGuardAuditContract.substrate: one migrated real PostgreSQL 16 container, shared by P21E-1, P21E-2, P21E-3 and P21E-4 within a single test
identityGuardAuditContract.additiveOnly: auditIdentityGuard is a fourth, optional pipeline option. The three required options, the four outcomes, the fixed stage order, the error envelope shape and the four write intents are unchanged, a pipeline built without the option behaves exactly as it did at this base, and the frozen test asserts that directly
identityGuardAuditContract.guardPrecedencePreserved: the tenant guard still decides ahead of the actor guard, so a request whose tenant and actor are both wrong is still the cross-tenant refusal it always was — and is now recorded under the cross-tenant reason, so that fixed precedence is visible in the log as well as in the response
identityGuardAuditContract.zeroCollaboratorCallsOnGuardDeny: an identity-guard refusal still reaches neither the policy decision point's candidate evaluation nor the invariant stage; the witness is the only collaborator a guard deny calls, and it is called exactly once with exactly one argument
identityGuardAuditContract.witnessSeesOnlyTheAuthenticatedIdentity: the argument is one frozen ordinary object carrying exactly code, principal, correlationId and idempotencyKey. `principal` is the exact Principal `identity.current()` answered, never the identity the ActionSpec claimed, and no claimed tenant or actor is placed in the object at all — the non-leak property holds by construction rather than by filtering
identityGuardAuditContract.awaitedNotMerelyCalled: the refusal is not projected until the audit has settled: run() stays pending while the witness is outstanding, and a witness that rejects propagates its refusal unchanged instead of returning an unrecorded deny envelope
identityGuardAuditContract.optionAdmission: keys are counted with Reflect.ownKeys so a symbol-keyed member is an unknown option rather than an unannounced one, every unknown key is refused, all three required options stay required, and the optional key is decided from its own property descriptor — an accessor is refused without ever being invoked, a non-enumerable member does not satisfy the option, and a present-but-undefined member is refused rather than silently read as absence
identityGuardAuditContract.optionAdmissionResidual: this is a shape and type gate, not a semantic one: a function of the right arity that records nothing, or records somewhere else, is admitted here and is not detectable from the pipeline. That is unchanged from the three options that were always required and is not claimed to be closed
identityGuardAuditContract.durableWitnessWiring: createAuditedCustomerComposition builds the witness from exactly the collaborators it already holds — the caller-supplied idGenerator, the Clock over the caller-supplied now, the one DecisionLogPort over PostgresDecisionLogAdapter.append, and the adapter's bound chainHead — so a guard refusal and a policy decision share one hash chain in the order they happened and one close still releases both owned pools
identityGuardAuditContract.auditOnlyDecisionShape: the witness reconstructs the decision that was never taken: one genuine customer.create Command over an empty payload, built only from the authenticated Principal and this request's own genuine CorrelationId and IdempotencyKey; one PolicyRequest whose resource names the authenticated tenant and whose context carries exactly the guard stage under `stage` (`identityTenantGuard`) and the code that refused under `guard`; and one fixed reserved system-layer default deny PolicyDecision that matches no policy and therefore resolves no layer, tracing this request's own CorrelationId. `matchedPolicyId` and `layerResolved` are both null because DecisionLogEntry admits a non-null layer only for a matched policy, and the guard matched none — the system-layer character of the refusal is carried in the fixed reason and the guard stage instead of in a fabricated policy id
identityGuardAuditContract.distinctReasonsPerGuard: the two guards carry two fixed, distinct reasons, so a cross-tenant reach and an actor mismatch are distinguishable in the log rather than collapsed into one; an unrecognised code is refused by the witness rather than filed under a blank reason
identityGuardAuditContract.failClosed: with the decision log's INSERT grant revoked on the live substrate the append refuses, the witness rejects, the pipeline rejects and the handler propagates: no deny envelope is answered, no decision row survives and no business row is written. Restoring the grant proves the same guard audit still works and still chains on, so the refusal is load-bearing rather than a harness that had stopped being able to write
identityGuardAuditContract.legacyCompositionStaysUnaudited: createCustomerComposition wires no witness and no decision log at all; its refusal is byte-for-byte what it was at this base and it still records nothing, which is exactly why the collaborator is injected by the audited factory rather than by the pipeline
identityGuardAuditContract.asgiFollowsWithoutNewWiring: createAuditedCustomerAsgiComposition is not touched by this package; because it composes createAuditedCustomerComposition, a cross-tenant claim taken straight off an attacker-controlled header is audited under the authenticated identity with no further wiring
identityGuardAuditContract.nonLeakSweepMethod: every column of every row of the decision log and the three write tables is projected to text through to_jsonb and searched for each attacker-claimed value, so a claimed tenant or actor cannot survive in a payload, a reason, a resource, a context or a column the test never thought to read
identityGuardAuditContract.countingMethod: whole-database count(*) over each write table as the superuser, with no tenant filter and no row-level predicate, so no row can hide behind a scope
identityGuardAuditContract.expectedValuesOwnedBy: the frozen test file only: status, outcome, error code, guard argument keys, decision payload fields, chain linkage and row counts are written there and are never read back out of this manifest
identityGuardAuditContract.manifestRole: the manifest is a load-bearing gate: the frozen test refuses to run any P21E scenario unless this file exists and declares exactly the five scenario ids in order

userJourney.once: CRM formundan gelen bir istek, başka bir şirketin (kiracının) müşterisiymiş gibi davranmaya kalktığında sistem onu doğru şekilde geri çeviriyordu — ama hiçbir yere hiçbir kayıt düşmüyordu. Kimlik koruması, yetki kararının verildiği aşamadan önce devreye girdiği için ortada deftere yazılacak bir 'karar' hiç oluşmuyordu. Yani kayda geçmesi en çok gereken istek türü, tam da hiç iz bırakmayan türdü.
userJourney.simdi: Kimlik koruması bir isteği geri çevirdiğinde, bu ret artık geri döndürülmeden önce aynı zincirli, yalnızca-ekleme yapılan karar defterine yazılıyor. Satır her zaman gerçekten doğrulanmış kimliğin altına düşüyor; isteğin iddia ettiği yabancı şirket veya yabancı kullanıcı bilgisi defterin hiçbir sütununa, hiçbir gerekçeye, hiçbir alana girmiyor. Yazma başarısızsa istek reddedilme yanıtı bile almıyor; hiçbir satır kalmıyor.
userJourney.fark: Sessizlik bitti. Yabancı şirket adına yapılan ilk deneme defterin ilk halkası oluyor ve kendi içeriğinden yeniden hesaplanan özetle bağımsızca doğrulanabiliyor. Yanlış kullanıcı denemesi ayrı bir gerekçeyle bir sonraki halkaya bağlanıyor, ikisi birden yanlışsa kayıt 'şirket uyuşmazlığı' olarak düşüyor — yani sistemin hangi kontrolü önce yaptığı defterden de okunabiliyor. Dürüst istek ise hiçbir şey değişmemiş gibi çalışıyor: kural denetimi yapılıyor, kayıt tamamlanıyor, makbuz dönüyor. Denetimsiz eski kurulum ise satırı satırına aynı kaldı ve hâlâ hiçbir şey yazmıyor.
userJourney.kullaniciYolculugu: CRM formu gönder → istek sınırdan girer → kimlik kontrolü yapılır → kimlik uymuyorsa: ret önce deftere yazılır, yazma bitmeden yanıt dönmez; yazma başarılıysa 403 reddi döner ve üç iş tablosuna tek satır düşmez; yazma başarısızsa istek hiçbir yanıt almaz ve hiçbir satır kalmaz → kimlik uyuyorsa: yetki kararı verilir ve o da aynı deftere yazılır → izin verilmişse kural denetimi çalışır, kayıt tek işlemde tamamlanır ve makbuz döner → istek bittiğinde tek bir kapatma çağrısı her iki bağlantı havuzunu da bırakır.
userJourney.kalanEngel: Bu hâlâ bir sınır ve veritabanı kanıtıdır, barındırılan bir ürün değildir. Seçilmiş bir sunucu, ağ dinleyicisi ve gerçek bir giriş/oturum akışı yok; 'doğrulanmış kimlik'in kim olduğunu hâlâ çağıran taraf söylüyor ve yetki kuralları hâlâ çağıranın verdiği adaylardan geliyor. Karar defterinin sorgulama, raporlama, saklama-süresi ve dışa aktarma yüzeyi yok. Seçenek kapısı biçim ve tür kontrolüdür: doğru türde ama hiçbir şey yazmayan bir tanık buradan ayırt edilemez.
